text:
maya: heads-up ran an orthogonalization probe on cassini-lite (quant6) against longtail-100k, results are surprising — small clusters look fine but a lot of orthogonal spiral clusters formed and recall@1 dropped.
julian: can you paste the eval command and a tiny digest of numbers?
maya: sure, ran this:
```bash
./tools/run_embed_eval --model cassini-lite-quant6 --dataset longtail-100k --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette --seed 42
```
maya: topline numbers: recall@1 -6.2% vs baseline, recall@5 -3.8%, recall@10 -2.1%, silhouette score -0.08 (baseline 0.21 -> 0.13)
maya: also checked mean cosine: baseline 0.37 -> cassini-lite 0.22, mean L2 norm increased 1.02 -> 1.38
eval-bot: eval finished: s3://redwood-evals/cassini-lite/orthoprobe/6171235678/summary.json (checksum abc123)
priya: hmm mean cosine that low + higher norms sounds like directional collapse away from dense islands — maybe quantization induced anisotropy. did you run with per-channel scale vs per-tensor?
maya: yes ran per-channel symmetric quant; also tried per-tensor asymmetric (quick) and the recall hit was slightly better but still ~-3% at r@1
alex: can you dump nearest neighbors for a handful of probes? curious if short queries get pushed to different clusters
maya: pasted a couple examples below (query -> top3 ids with cos):
- "how to reset password" -> [doc_342 (0.81), doc_114 (0.79), doc_903 (0.76)] (baseline similar)
- "api rate limits" -> [doc_778 (0.34), doc_221 (0.31), doc_499 (0.30)] (baseline had 0.62,0.60,0.58)
julian: ok clear longtail queries are affected. can you run the same eval but with whitening turned off and with global mean-centering?
maya: queued both jobs. planning UMAP of 5k sample to visualize cluster shapes.
priya: also try removing L2-normalization at indexing time (we index with cosine currently). if quantization pushes norms around, L2-norm normalization pre-index might help.
alex: +1 to try whitening + pre-normalize. Also run per-language split check (en/es/zh) — sometimes quant interacts with tokenization/length distributions.
maya: running: 1) whitening+pre-normalize, 2) no-normalize index, 3) per-lang splits. will post artifacts.
julian: thanks. if those don't fix, next step is to try 8-bit quant fallback for the encoder (hybrid FP16/INT8) and re-run small sample.
maya: noted. will update when jobs finish. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
